evidence.text: Construct Dirac zero modes by mixing internal spinor components when oblique fluxes obstruct single-component solutions. Establish the proposed basis through field equations, torus transition laws, and orthonormality integrals using Fourier and Gaussian sums.

evidence.text: Solve section-degree constraints without denominator coordinates, extract minimal divisor factors, and identify the candidate fiber. Check monodromy and matter separately before concluding non-Higgsability.

sources.title: Type IIB string theory, S-duality, and generalized cohomology

sources.title: Flux-vacua in two dimensional string theory

evidence.text: Chiral quantization uses u=(p−x)/√2 and s=(p+x)/√2 as incoming and outgoing bases. Fourier transforms encode 0B scattering, while Bessel kernels occur in 0A. Products of one-particle amplitudes and scattering-phase densities yield transition amplitudes and thermal free energies.

sources.title: The Uncertainty of Fluxes

evidence.text: Compute the Maxwell Poisson kernel and its annihilator to identify symplectic leaves labeled by real magnetic/electric fluxes. Integration by parts gives commuting classical fluxes; quantization of a leaf uses a Fock representation and Hamiltonian polarization.
